name: Capability Lattice Collapse
research_question: Can individually authorized ClayCode effects compose inside a dynamic Assembly into a stronger unauthorized end-to-end capability even when every local effect check passes?

hypotheses.text: Per-effect capability checks are insufficient if a dynamic Assembly can compose protected-source access with an independently authorized sink while provenance/information-flow labels are not preserved end-to-end.
A joint commit-time authority-closure check over capability provenance and protected information-flow labels can block this amplification without requiring a broad ClayCode semantic redesign.

counterhypotheses.text: The existing Safe-Effect Geometry plus external capability/effect gateway already entails the needed end-to-end confinement, so the finding is only an implementation/conformance test requirement rather than a new semantic mechanism.
Assembly-level checks may be unnecessary if protected values are unforgeable typed resources whose authorized adapters never materialize bearer values into general Workspace payloads.

cross_connections: claycode: CC-WP-04 TYPE-EFFECT, CC-WP-07 RUNTIME-ABI-FFI, CC-WP-09 CONCURRENCY-MEMORY, CC-WP-11 FUZZ-CONFORMANCE
gwt/emergenz: dynamic Assembly interaction can create a joint system effect not present in isolated factors; causal-use/outcome receipts must not become authority
safe-effect geometry: authority non-amplification and protected information-flow confinement already define the target invariants

experiment.interpretation: This is an existence counterexample to the sufficiency of independent local effect authorization under lossy provenance. It does not establish a vulnerability in current ClayCode because the BASE compiler/runtime/type-effect implementation is not yet complete.
experiment.negative_result: No evidence was found that this requires a new permanent scientific branch or immediate ClayCode semantic redesign; current project foundations already contain authority non-amplification and protected information-flow confinement invariants.

architecture_implication: Treat dynamic Assembly composition as an authority-closure boundary. Before external commit, compute effective source labels, sink policy, capability provenance and external grants; reject any composite flow outside the declared protected-invariant envelope. Prefer implementing this in the type/effect checker + deterministic runtime/effect gateway and proving it with conformance/fuzz tests before changing ClayCode core semantics.
falsifier: If the frozen ClayCode/FRANK contracts can prove that protected values never enter general Assembly payloads and all sinks enforce purpose-bound source provenance through unforgeable types, then the extra joint gate is redundant and the field should close as NO_CHANGE beyond test coverage.
